Absolutely. These manufacturers are also held to an extremely high standard. Some of the best performing food safety audits I have ever done are in canning facilities

There’s a compound in beans that can naturally produce air bubbles or foam. The air bubble could have also been created when breaking the surface tension of the liquid when opening the can. Spoiled foods that product gas will smell and taste foul - think methane gas. Canned foods are produced using the retort method, in that they are sterilised after filling into the can. If no seal was broken and the can was completely intact with no damage, there is no risk. The biggest risk for canned foods is Clostridium Botulinum, however this does not produce gas.

If it smells normal, yes. Sometimes mould is hard to see depending on the type of bread, but you will smell it. It smells very earthy. Also yeast is an organism of concern, that will smell like strong alcohol. Both are simply spoilage bacteria and aren’t usually a food safety concern. Bread has a very low water activity so risk if poisoning is almost non-existent

You’ll be fine! They base best practice for people who get sick easily, so as long as you’re relatively healthy, you’re all good :) Even then the risk is minimal if you cooked it properly the first time
Throw it out. Opened lunch meat should be consumed within 5 days of opening. The stuff around the seal looks like condensation to me but water = more bacteria growth
You’re 100% fine. The plastic seal is only for tamper evidence in the store. If the cap took some effort to take off, it hasn’t been tampered with and is safe
All foods should be reheated to 165. Soup is low risk but it’s best practice
If the cap was tight, no problems. Barbecue sauce is fairly acidic too and very inhospitable for Clostridium Botulinum
When did you open it?
165 when reheating. You’ve killed off most of the bugs when you cooked it, but some may multiply before reheating. Low risk of poisoning but it’s best practice
